rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials across three tracks ended off_track with zero finishes. Iteration 2 cut kp from 3.0 to 1.5 and added kd, which raised scores (59.3 to 64.1), but max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.067, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit (for body_width 0.12 the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06). Steering_oscillation is still 0.11 to 0.16 and line losses are 1 to 2 per run. Progress is only 0.12 to 0.19, so runs die within the first metre.

Diagnosis: max_error is nearly unchanged across the kp change, so steering gain is not the main limit. The likely causes are (a) sensor lag, since sensors at y = 0.05 see the curve late and the loop reacts after the robot has drifted, and (b) a narrow sensor cluster (0.048 m span with 0.012 m sensors) that loses the tape on tight bends, which causes the line-loss events. The high oscillation with kd = 0.5 also suggests that derivative action amplifies sensor noise, so I am bringing kd back down.

Changes: (1) Move the sensors forward to y = 0.07 so the line is read earlier, which gives the loop more time to react. (2) Widen the array to x = -0.03 to +0.03 with 0.015 m spacing, so the outer sensors keep the tape in view on bends and line loss is less likely. (3) Lower kp from 1.5 to 1.2 and kd from 0.5 to 0.4 to reduce jitter. (4) Keep ki at 0.05. (5) Lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3 so the robot has more time to correct at bends and stays on the tape. The trade-off is a slower lap, which I accept because surviving the course is worth more than finish time right now. Wheel geometry, mass and body are unchanged, since body_width 0.18 would only raise the off-track limit to 0.0575, which gains nothing.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06, fewer line-loss events (target 0 to 1), lower steering_oscillation, and progress above 0.3, with a first chance at completion on the oval and s-bend. The slalom may still be the hardest track. The next telemetry should show whether the forward sensor placement reduced max_error and whether the lower base_speed kept the robot on the line.
